note: TOEFL iBT Listening, 2026 format (owner 2026-11-01), American voices: Listen and Choose a Response (en_reply), conversations (en_q), announcements (en_talk, part 3), academic talks (en_talk, part 4); every recording once. Round 1: 8 + 6 + 4 + 6 = 24 questions. Original texts. Drafted in tools/.mockups/us_ls.py.

lines.s: Do you know if the library is open late tonight?
lines.zh: 你知道圖書館今晚有開到很晚嗎？
lines.en: Do you know if the library is open late tonight?

options.t: I think it closes at midnight during exam week.
options.zh: 我想考試週會開到半夜十二點。
options.en: I think it closes at midnight during exam week.

options.t: Yes, I was late for class.
options.en: Yes, I was late for class.

explain.zh: 問圖書館開到多晚，回答「考試週開到半夜」最切題。
explain.en: It answers how late the library is open.

lines.s: I can't believe the professor moved the deadline up.
lines.zh: 真不敢相信教授把截止日提前了。
lines.en: I can't believe the professor moved the deadline up.

options.t: He's teaching two classes this term.
options.en: He's teaching two classes this term.

options.t: The paper is about climate change.
options.zh: 那篇報告是關於氣候變遷。
options.en: The paper is about climate change.

options.t: I know. Now we only have three days.
options.zh: 就是說，現在只剩三天了。
options.en: I know. Now we only have three days.

options.zh: 我們把桌子搬到樓上吧。

explain.zh: move up 是「提前」。同意並說「只剩三天」最自然；(D) 用 move 混淆。

lines.s: Have you decided which lab section you're signing up for?
lines.zh: 你決定要選哪一個實驗課時段了嗎？
lines.en: Have you decided which lab section you're signing up for?

options.t: The lab is in the science building.
options.en: The lab is in the science building.

options.t: Probably the Tuesday one. It fits my schedule.
options.zh: 大概星期二那個，跟我的課表配得上。
options.en: Probably the Tuesday one. It fits my schedule.

options.t: I signed the form for you.
options.en: I signed the form for you.

options.t: We did that experiment last week.
options.zh: 我們上週做過那個實驗了。
options.en: We did that experiment last week.

explain.zh: 問選哪個時段，答「星期二那個」。
explain.en: He asks which section; she names one.

lines.s: Would you mind if I borrowed your notes from Monday's lecture?
lines.zh: 我可以借你星期一那堂課的筆記嗎？
lines.en: Would you mind if I borrowed your notes from Monday's lecture?

options.t: Sure, I'll email you a copy tonight.
options.zh: 當然，我今晚寄一份給你。
options.en: Sure, I'll email you a copy tonight.

explain.zh: 對方借筆記，答應並說會寄給她。

lines.s: The bookstore said the textbook won't arrive until next week.
lines.zh: 書店說課本要到下週才會到。
lines.en: The bookstore said the textbook won't arrive until next week.

options.t: Maybe you can find a used copy online.
options.zh: 也許你可以在網路上找二手的。
options.en: Maybe you can find a used copy online.

options.t: The store is next to the cafeteria.
options.en: The store is next to the cafeteria.

explain.zh: 課本晚到是個問題，給他「找二手書」的建議最合適。
explain.en: A helpful suggestion for the problem.

lines.s: Why weren't you at the study group yesterday?
lines.zh: 你昨天為什麼沒來讀書會？
lines.en: Why weren't you at the study group yesterday?

options.t: I had to work an extra shift.
options.en: I had to work an extra shift.

explain.zh: 問「為什麼」，答原因「要多上一個班」。

lines.s: Are you going to apply for the summer internship?
lines.zh: 你要申請暑期實習嗎？
lines.en: Are you going to apply for the summer internship?

options.t: The application is two pages long.
options.en: The application is two pages long.

options.t: I already did. I'm waiting to hear back.
options.zh: 我已經申請了，在等回音。
options.en: I already did. I'm waiting to hear back.

lines.s: This campus is so much bigger than I expected.
lines.zh: 這個校園比我想像的大好多。
lines.en: This campus is so much bigger than I expected.

options.t: The campus map costs two dollars.
options.en: The campus map costs two dollars.

options.t: My dorm room is small too.
options.en: My dorm room is small too.

options.t: You'll get used to it. The shuttle bus helps a lot.

options.en: You'll get used to it. The shuttle bus helps a lot.

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the registrar's office.
lines.zh: 請聽一位學生和註冊組職員的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the registrar's office.

lines.s: Hi. I'm trying to add a course, but the online system says the class is full.
lines.zh: 你好。我想加選一門課，可是線上系統說已經額滿了。
lines.en: Hi. I'm trying to add a course, but the online system says the class is full.

lines.s: Which course is it?
lines.zh: 是哪一門課？
lines.en: Which course is it?

lines.s: Introduction to Psychology, the Wednesday evening section. I need it to graduate next spring.
lines.zh: 心理學概論，星期三晚上那班。我明年春天畢業需要這門課。
lines.en: Introduction to Psychology, the Wednesday evening section. I need it to graduate next spring.

lines.s: In that case, you can ask the professor for a permission form. If she signs it, we can add you even if the class is full.
lines.zh: 這樣的話，你可以向教授要一張許可單。只要她簽名，就算額滿我們也能幫你加選。
lines.en: In that case, you can ask the professor for a permission form. If she signs it, we can add you even if the class is full.

lines.s: Great. Her office hours are tomorrow, so I'll go then.
lines.zh: 太好了。她明天有辦公室時間，我那時候去。
lines.en: Great. Her office hours are tomorrow, so I'll go then.

ask.s: Why does the woman go to the registrar's office?
ask.zh: 女的為什麼去註冊組？
ask.en: Why does the woman go to the registrar's office?

options.t: To add a course that is full

explain.zh: 她想加選的課「已經額滿了」。
explain.en: She wants to add a full course.

ask.s: What will the woman probably do tomorrow?

ask.en: What will the woman probably do tomorrow?

lines.en: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.s: Good idea. I'll reserve one of the group study rooms.
lines.zh: 好主意。我來預約一間小組討論室。
lines.en: Good idea. I'll reserve one of the group study rooms.

ask.s: What does the woman say about the articles?
ask.zh: 關於那些文章，女的說了什麼？
ask.en: What does the woman say about the articles?

explain.zh: 「我來預約一間小組討論室」。

lines.zh: 請聽一位學生和宿舍輔導員的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and a resident advisor.

lines.en: Oh no. Did you fill out a maintenance request?

lines.zh: 有，星期一就填了，可是還沒有人來。
lines.en: I did, on Monday, but nobody's come yet.

ask.en: What is the man's problem?

ask.s: What does the woman offer to do?

ask.en: What does the woman offer to do?

explain.zh: 「我現在就打給維修處」。申請單他已經填過了。

lines.s: Listen to an announcement on a university campus.
lines.zh: 請聽一段校園廣播。
lines.en: Listen to an announcement on a university campus.

lines.s: Attention, students. Because of tomorrow's snowstorm, all classes before noon are cancelled. The library and the dining hall will open at eleven instead of their usual times. Afternoon classes will meet as scheduled unless your instructor tells you otherwise by e-mail. Please check the university website for updates.
lines.zh: 同學請注意。因為明天的暴風雪，中午以前的課全部停課。圖書館和餐廳改成十一點開放。下午的課照常上課，除非老師用電子郵件另行通知。請留意學校網站的最新消息。
lines.en: Attention, students. Because of tomorrow's snowstorm, all classes before noon are cancelled. The library and the dining hall will open at eleven instead of their usual times. Afternoon classes will meet as scheduled unless your instructor tells you otherwise by e-mail. Please check the university website for updates.

ask.zh: 這段廣播的主要目的是什麼？
ask.en: What is the main purpose of the announcement?

options.t: To announce changes caused by the weather
To explain how the website works

explain.zh: 因為暴風雪，宣布停課和開放時間的改變。

ask.s: What should students do about afternoon classes?
ask.zh: 下午的課，學生應該怎麼做？
ask.en: What should students do about afternoon classes?

options.t: Attend them unless told otherwise by e-mail

explain.zh: 「下午照常上課，除非老師用電子郵件另行通知」。
explain.en: Go, unless the instructor e-mails otherwise.

lines.s: Listen to an announcement in a class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段課堂上的宣布。
lines.en: Listen to an announcement in a class.

lines.s: Before we begin, a quick announcement about the field trip on the twelfth. The bus will leave from the front of the science building at eight sharp, so please don't be late. Bring a notebook and comfortable shoes, since we'll be walking along the river for about two hours. If you can't come, let me know by Friday, and I'll give you a different assignment.

lines.en: Before we begin, a quick announcement about the field trip on the twelfth. The bus will leave from the front of the science building at eight sharp, so please don't be late. Bring a notebook and comfortable shoes, since we'll be walking along the river for about two hours. If you can't come, let me know by Friday, and I'll give you a different assignment.

ask.s: What is the announcement mainly about?
ask.zh: 這段宣布主要是關於什麼？
ask.en: What is the announcement mainly about?

explain.zh: 「十二號的戶外教學」。
explain.en: The field trip on the twelfth.

ask.s: What should students who cannot attend do?
ask.zh: 不能參加的學生應該怎麼做？
ask.en: What should students who cannot attend do?

options.t: Write a report on the river

explain.zh: 「如果不能來，請在星期五前告訴我」。

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段生物課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

lines.s: Today let's look at a question scientists have studied for a long time: how do migrating birds find their way over thousands of kilometers? It turns out they use several tools. During the day, many birds use the position of the sun. At night, some species use the stars. In one famous experiment, young birds raised in a planetarium learned to find their direction from the artificial night sky. But perhaps the most surprising tool is the Earth's magnetic field. Researchers have found that birds can sense it, which helps them keep their direction even when the sky is cloudy. So migration isn't about one single sense. It's about combining information from different sources.
lines.zh: 今天來看一個科學家研究很久的問題：候鳥怎麼飛越幾千公里還找得到路？原來牠們用了好幾種工具。白天，很多鳥靠太陽的位置；晚上，有些鳥種靠星星。在一個有名的實驗裡，在天文館長大的幼鳥，學會了靠人造夜空辨認方向。不過最令人驚訝的工具，也許是地球的磁場。研究人員發現鳥能感覺到磁場，所以就算天空多雲也能維持方向。所以遷徙靠的不是單一感官，而是結合不同來源的資訊。
lines.en: Today let's look at a question scientists have studied for a long time: how do migrating birds find their way over thousands of kilometers? It turns out they use several tools. During the day, many birds use the position of the sun. At night, some species use the stars. In one famous experiment, young birds raised in a planetarium learned to find their direction from the artificial night sky. But perhaps the most surprising tool is the Earth's magnetic field. Researchers have found that birds can sense it, which helps them keep their direction even when the sky is cloudy. So migration isn't about one single sense. It's about combining information from different sources.

ask.s: What is the lecture mainly about?
ask.zh: 這段講課主要是關於什麼？
ask.en: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.t: How birds find their way when migrating
Why some birds do not migrate

explain.zh: 開頭就提出「候鳥怎麼找到路」，之後介紹各種方法。
explain.en: How migrating birds find their way.

ask.s: What did the planetarium experiment show?
ask.zh: 天文館的實驗顯示了什麼？
ask.en: What did the planetarium experiment show?

options.t: Birds prefer to fly at night.
Birds can learn to use the stars.

explain.zh: 幼鳥「學會了靠人造夜空辨認方向」。
explain.en: Young birds learned direction from the artificial sky.

ask.s: Why does the professor mention cloudy skies?
ask.zh: 教授為什麼提到多雲的天空？
ask.en: Why does the professor mention cloudy skies?

options.t: To describe bad weather during migration
To explain why the magnetic field is useful
To show that birds stop flying

explain.zh: 靠磁場，「就算天空多雲也能維持方向」，說明磁場的用處。
explain.en: The magnetic field still works when the sun and stars are hidden.

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in a history class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段歷史課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in a history class.

lines.s: In the late sixteen hundreds, coffee houses became extremely popular in London. They were sometimes called penny universities, because for the price of a cup of coffee, about a penny, anyone could sit and listen to conversations about politics, science and business. Some coffee houses even became the starting point for major institutions. For example, merchants who met at one coffee house to share news about ships eventually formed one of the world's largest insurance markets. So these weren't just places to drink coffee. They were centers for exchanging information.
lines.zh: 十七世紀後期，咖啡館在倫敦非常流行。人們有時稱它們為「一便士大學」，因為只要一杯咖啡的錢，大約一便士，任何人都能坐下來聽人談政治、科學和生意。有些咖啡館甚至成了重要機構的起點。例如，在某家咖啡館聚會交換船隻消息的商人，後來組成了世界上最大的保險市場之一。所以這些地方不只是喝咖啡的地方，而是交換資訊的中心。
lines.en: In the late sixteen hundreds, coffee houses became extremely popular in London. They were sometimes called penny universities, because for the price of a cup of coffee, about a penny, anyone could sit and listen to conversations about politics, science and business. Some coffee houses even became the starting point for major institutions. For example, merchants who met at one coffee house to share news about ships eventually formed one of the world's largest insurance markets. So these weren't just places to drink coffee. They were centers for exchanging information.

ask.s: What is the main topic of the lecture?
ask.zh: 這段講課的主題是什麼？
ask.en: What is the main topic of the lecture?

options.t: The role of early coffee houses in London

explain.zh: 講的是十七世紀倫敦咖啡館的角色。
explain.en: Early London coffee houses and what they did.

ask.s: Why were coffee houses called "penny universities"?
ask.zh: 咖啡館為什麼被稱為「一便士大學」？
ask.en: Why were coffee houses called "penny universities"?

options.t: People could learn from conversations for the price of a coffee.
Books were sold there for a penny.

explain.zh: 只要「一杯咖啡的錢」就能聽人談政治、科學和生意。
explain.en: For a penny, anyone could listen and learn.

ask.s: What does the professor say about the merchants?
ask.zh: 教授說那些商人怎麼了？
ask.en: What does the professor say about the merchants?

options.t: They opened the first coffee house.
Their meetings led to an insurance market.

explain.zh: 他們在咖啡館交換船隻消息，「後來組成了保險市場」。
explain.en: Their meetings grew into an insurance market.

lines.s: Are you going to the career fair this afternoon?
lines.zh: 你今天下午要去就業博覽會嗎？
lines.en: Are you going to the career fair this afternoon?

options.t: I'm planning to, after my lab.
options.zh: 打算去，等我上完實驗課。
options.en: I'm planning to, after my lab.

options.t: It was on the bulletin board.
options.en: It was on the bulletin board.

explain.zh: 問今天下午會不會去，回答「打算去，上完實驗課後」。
explain.en: He plans to go after his lab.

lines.s: I can't find the reading list for the history course.
lines.zh: 我找不到歷史課的閱讀書單。
lines.en: I can't find the reading list for the history course.

options.zh: 歷史是我最喜歡的科目。

options.t: It's posted on the course website.
options.en: It's posted on the course website.

lines.s: Would you mind lending me your notes from Tuesday's lecture?
lines.zh: 你介意借我星期二講課的筆記嗎？
lines.en: Would you mind lending me your notes from Tuesday's lecture?

options.t: Not at all. I'll e-mail them to you.
options.zh: 一點也不。我寄電子郵件給你。
options.en: Not at all. I'll e-mail them to you.

options.t: Tuesday is fine for the exam.
options.en: Tuesday is fine for the exam.

explain.zh: 「Would you mind…?」回答「Not at all」表示願意。

lines.s: The dining hall is serving a special dinner for international students tonight.

lines.en: The dining hall is serving a special dinner for international students tonight.

options.t: I study in the international office.
options.en: I study in the international office.

lines.s: How did your presentation go?
lines.zh: 你的報告進行得怎麼樣？
lines.en: How did your presentation go?

options.t: I presented it in room twelve.
options.en: I presented it in room twelve.

explain.zh: 問結果，回答「比預期好」。

lines.s: Do you know whether the bookstore buys back used textbooks?
lines.zh: 你知道書店有沒有回收二手課本嗎？
lines.en: Do you know whether the bookstore buys back used textbooks?

options.t: The bookstore is near the gym.
options.en: The bookstore is near the gym.

options.t: Only at the end of each semester.
options.en: Only at the end of each semester.

explain.zh: 問有沒有回收，回答「只在每學期末」。

lines.s: I think I'm going to drop my statistics class.
lines.zh: 我想我要退選統計課。
lines.en: I think I'm going to drop my statistics class.

explain.zh: 對方說要退選，自然的回應是問原因。(C) 用 dropped 混淆。

lines.s: The professor said the exam will cover chapters one through five.
lines.zh: 教授說考試範圍是第一到第五章。
lines.en: The professor said the exam will cover chapters one through five.

options.t: Then I'd better start reviewing tonight.
options.zh: 那我最好今晚就開始複習。
options.en: Then I'd better start reviewing tonight.

explain.zh: 知道考試範圍，回應「今晚就開始複習」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.
lines.zh: 請聽一段學生和圖書館員的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.

lines.s: Hi, I need a book for my sociology paper, but the system says it's checked out.
lines.zh: 你好，我的社會學報告需要一本書，但系統說借出去了。
lines.en: Hi, I need a book for my sociology paper, but the system says it's checked out.

lines.s: You can place a hold on it. When it's returned, we'll e-mail you, and you'll have three days to pick it up.
lines.zh: 你可以預約。還回來時我們會寄電子郵件，你有三天可以來拿。
lines.en: You can place a hold on it. When it's returned, we'll e-mail you, and you'll have three days to pick it up.

lines.s: My paper is due on Friday, though.
lines.zh: 可是我的報告星期五要交。
lines.en: My paper is due on Friday, though.

lines.s: In that case, try our electronic database. Many sociology books are available online.
lines.zh: 那你可以試試我們的電子資料庫，很多社會學書都能在線上看。
lines.en: In that case, try our electronic database. Many sociology books are available online.

ask.s: What is the student's problem?
ask.zh: 學生有什麼問題？
ask.en: What is the student's problem?

options.t: A book he needs is checked out.

ask.s: What does the librarian finally suggest?
ask.zh: 圖書館員最後建議什麼？
ask.en: What does the librarian finally suggest?

options.t: Asking his professor for more time

explain.zh: 「試試我們的電子資料庫」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.en: Yes. My current roommate is graduating. Do you know anyone?

lines.s: My friend Leo is. He's quiet and he studies a lot, but he plays the guitar in the evenings.
lines.zh: 我朋友里歐在找。他很安靜，很認真讀書，不過晚上會彈吉他。
lines.en: My friend Leo is. He's quiet and he studies a lot, but he plays the guitar in the evenings.

lines.zh: 沒關係，我反正通常在圖書館待到九點。可以給我他的電話嗎？
lines.en: That's fine — I'm usually at the library until nine anyway. Could you give me his number?

Buses will leave every forty minutes instead of every fifteen, and the last bus will depart from the main gate at eight p.m. Students who need transportation later than that may request a ride from campus security.

ask.zh: 下週一會有什麼改變？
ask.en: What will change next Monday?

ask.s: What can students do if they need a ride after 8 p.m.?

ask.en: What can students do if they need a ride after 8 p.m.?

lines.s: Listen to an announcement in a class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段課堂上的宣布。
lines.en: Listen to an announcement in a class.

lines.s: Before we start, a reminder about your group projects. Each group should send me a one-page proposal by Thursday at noon. Next week we'll meet in the computer lab instead of this room, so you can work on your data together. And don't forget to bring your student ID — you'll need it to log in.
lines.zh: 開始之前，提醒大家小組報告的事。每組要在星期四中午前寄給我一頁的提案。下週我們改在電腦教室上課，不在這間，方便大家一起處理資料。別忘了帶學生證，登入要用。
lines.en: Before we start, a reminder about your group projects. Each group should send me a one-page proposal by Thursday at noon. Next week we'll meet in the computer lab instead of this room, so you can work on your data together. And don't forget to bring your student ID — you'll need it to log in.

ask.s: What must each group send by Thursday?
ask.zh: 每組星期四前要寄什麼？
ask.en: What must each group send by Thursday?

explain.zh: 「一頁的提案」。

ask.s: Why should students bring their student ID next week?
ask.zh: 下週為什麼要帶學生證？
ask.en: Why should students bring their student ID next week?

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段環境科學課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class.

lines.s: Let's talk about urban heat islands. Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them. Why? Dark surfaces such as asphalt and roofs absorb sunlight during the day and release that heat slowly at night. Cities also have fewer trees, and trees cool the air by releasing water from their leaves. Some cities are fighting back by painting roofs white and planting rooftop gardens. In one study, a white roof stayed about thirty degrees cooler than a dark one on a summer afternoon.
lines.zh: 我們來談城市熱島。城市常常比周圍的鄉村熱好幾度。為什麼？柏油路和屋頂這類深色表面白天吸收陽光，晚上慢慢把熱放出來。城市的樹也比較少，而樹會透過葉子釋放水分讓空氣變涼。有些城市開始反擊，把屋頂漆成白色、種屋頂花園。一項研究中，夏天下午白色屋頂比深色屋頂涼了大約三十度。
lines.en: Let's talk about urban heat islands. Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them. Why? Dark surfaces such as asphalt and roofs absorb sunlight during the day and release that heat slowly at night. Cities also have fewer trees, and trees cool the air by releasing water from their leaves. Some cities are fighting back by painting roofs white and planting rooftop gardens. In one study, a white roof stayed about thirty degrees cooler than a dark one on a summer afternoon.

ask.s: What is the lecture mainly about?
ask.zh: 這段講課主要是關於什麼？
ask.en: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.t: Why cities are warmer than the countryside

explain.zh: 講的是城市熱島：城市為什麼比較熱。

ask.s: According to the professor, how do trees cool the air?
ask.zh: 教授說樹怎麼讓空氣變涼？
ask.en: According to the professor, how do trees cool the air?

options.t: By releasing water from their leaves

explain.zh: 「透過葉子釋放水分」。

ask.s: Why does the professor mention a study?
ask.zh: 教授為什麼提到一項研究？
ask.en: Why does the professor mention a study?

options.t: To explain how heat islands form
To show how effective white roofs can be

explain.zh: 研究顯示白色屋頂涼很多，說明效果。

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in a psychology class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段心理學課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in a psychology class.

lines.s: Today's topic is memory and sleep. For a long time, people thought sleep was simply rest for the brain. We now know the brain is very active during sleep. In one experiment, students learned a list of words, then half of them slept and half stayed awake. The next day, those who slept remembered far more. Researchers believe that during deep sleep the brain replays what we learned and moves it into long-term memory. So staying up all night before an exam may actually hurt your score.
lines.zh: 今天的主題是記憶與睡眠。長久以來大家以為睡覺只是讓大腦休息。現在我們知道睡眠時大腦非常活躍。一項實驗中，學生學一串單字，之後一半睡覺、一半熬夜。隔天睡覺的那組記得多得多。研究者認為深層睡眠時，大腦會重播學過的東西，把它轉進長期記憶。所以考前熬夜其實可能讓分數變差。
lines.en: Today's topic is memory and sleep. For a long time, people thought sleep was simply rest for the brain. We now know the brain is very active during sleep. In one experiment, students learned a list of words, then half of them slept and half stayed awake. The next day, those who slept remembered far more. Researchers believe that during deep sleep the brain replays what we learned and moves it into long-term memory. So staying up all night before an exam may actually hurt your score.

ask.s: What did people believe about sleep in the past?
ask.zh: 過去人們怎麼看睡眠？
ask.en: What did people believe about sleep in the past?

options.t: It was simply rest for the brain.

explain.zh: 「以為睡覺只是讓大腦休息」。

ask.s: What happened in the experiment?
ask.zh: 實驗結果如何？
ask.en: What happened in the experiment?

options.t: Students who stayed awake did better.

explain.zh: 「睡覺的那組記得多得多」。

ask.s: What does the professor imply about studying all night?
ask.zh: 教授暗示整夜讀書會怎樣？
ask.en: What does the professor imply about studying all night?

options.t: It is the best way to prepare.

explain.zh: 「考前熬夜其實可能讓分數變差」。

lines.s: Is the writing center open on weekends?
lines.zh: 寫作中心週末有開嗎？
lines.en: Is the writing center open on weekends?

options.t: The center is across from the gym.
options.en: The center is across from the gym.

explain.zh: 問週末有沒有開，回答「只有星期六上午」。

lines.s: I missed the bus, so I'll be late for our study group.
lines.zh: 我錯過公車了，所以讀書會會遲到。
lines.en: I missed the bus, so I'll be late for our study group.

options.t: No problem. We'll wait for you.
options.en: No problem. We'll wait for you.

explain.zh: 對方說會遲到，回應「沒關係，我們等妳」。

lines.s: Which section of chemistry are you taking?
lines.zh: 你上哪一班的化學？
lines.en: Which section of chemistry are you taking?

options.t: The lab is on the fourth floor.
options.en: The lab is on the fourth floor.

options.t: The one on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
options.en: The one on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

explain.zh: 問哪一班，回答時段。

lines.s: Have you decided on a topic for your research paper?
lines.zh: 你決定研究報告的題目了嗎？
lines.en: Have you decided on a topic for your research paper?

options.t: Not yet. I'm choosing between two ideas.
options.zh: 還沒，我在兩個想法之間選。
options.en: Not yet. I'm choosing between two ideas.

explain.zh: 問決定了沒，回答「還沒，在兩個想法間選」。

lines.s: The music department is giving a free concert on Friday.
lines.zh: 音樂系星期五有免費音樂會。
lines.en: The music department is giving a free concert on Friday.

options.t: Sounds great. What time does it start?
options.en: Sounds great. What time does it start?

options.t: Friday is my day off from work.
options.en: Friday is my day off from work.

explain.zh: 對消息有興趣，接著問時間最自然。
explain.en: Showing interest and asking the time.

lines.s: My laptop crashed and I lost my essay.

lines.en: My laptop crashed and I lost my essay.

options.t: Did you save a copy online?
options.en: Did you save a copy online?

explain.zh: 對方遺失論文，回應「有沒有線上備份」。(D) 用 crashed 混淆。

lines.s: Do you want to join the hiking club with me?
lines.zh: 妳要跟我一起加入登山社嗎？
lines.en: Do you want to join the hiking club with me?

options.t: I'd love to, but I'm busy on weekends.
options.en: I'd love to, but I'm busy on weekends.

explain.zh: 邀請，回答「很想但週末很忙」。

lines.s: The registration deadline for spring courses is tomorrow.
lines.zh: 春季課程報名截止日是明天。
lines.en: The registration deadline for spring courses is tomorrow.

options.zh: 春天是我最喜歡的季節。

options.t: Thanks for reminding me. I haven't signed up yet.
options.en: Thanks for reminding me. I haven't signed up yet.

explain.zh: 收到提醒，回應「謝謝提醒，我還沒報名」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between a student and an adviser.
lines.zh: 請聽一段學生和輔導員的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and an adviser.

lines.zh: 我在考慮明年出國交換，但擔心會延畢。
lines.en: I'm thinking about studying abroad next year, but I'm worried it will delay my graduation.

lines.zh: 不一定。我們很多姊妹校的課可以抵主修學分。

lines.en: Check the study-abroad website, then bring me a list of courses you're interested in. I'll confirm them with your department.

ask.s: What is the student worried about?

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.en: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in an art history class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段藝術史課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in an art history class.

lines.s: When we look at old paintings, we often see colors that seem dull. But many of them were once much brighter. Some pigments used by painters, like certain yellows and reds, fade when exposed to light over centuries. Others change color because of chemical reactions with the air. Today, museums protect paintings by keeping the lights low and controlling the humidity. Scientists can even use X-rays to discover the original colors hidden underneath.
lines.zh: 我們看古畫時，常常覺得顏色很暗淡。但很多畫以前鮮豔得多。畫家用的某些顏料，例如某些黃色和紅色，經過幾世紀照光就會褪色；另一些則因為和空氣起化學反應而變色。現在博物館用低亮度的燈光和控制濕度來保護畫作。科學家甚至能用 X 光找出底下原本的顏色。
lines.en: When we look at old paintings, we often see colors that seem dull. But many of them were once much brighter. Some pigments used by painters, like certain yellows and reds, fade when exposed to light over centuries. Others change color because of chemical reactions with the air. Today, museums protect paintings by keeping the lights low and controlling the humidity. Scientists can even use X-rays to discover the original colors hidden underneath.

ask.s: What is the lecture mainly about?
ask.zh: 這段講課主要是關於什麼？
ask.en: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.t: Why the colors of old paintings change
The life of a famous painter

explain.zh: 講古畫顏色為什麼改變。

ask.s: What causes some pigments to fade?
ask.zh: 什麼讓某些顏料褪色？
ask.en: What causes some pigments to fade?

explain.zh: 「照光就會褪色」。

ask.s: How do scientists discover the original colors?
ask.zh: 科學家怎麼找出原本的顏色？
ask.en: How do scientists discover the original colors?

explain.zh: 「用 X 光找出底下原本的顏色」。

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in a business class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段商業課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in a business class.

lines.s: Let's discuss why some small businesses succeed where large companies fail. Take local bookstores. Ten years ago, many people predicted online retailers would close them all. Instead, a lot of independent bookstores are doing well. Why? They offer something online shops can't: personal recommendations from staff, author events and a sense of community. In other words, they stopped competing on price and started competing on experience.
lines.zh: 我們來討論為什麼有些小商家能在大公司失敗的地方成功。以在地書店為例。十年前很多人預測網路零售商會讓書店全部倒閉。結果很多獨立書店經營得很好。為什麼？它們提供網路商店做不到的東西：店員的個人推薦、作家活動和社群感。換句話說，它們不再拚價格，而是拚體驗。
lines.en: Let's discuss why some small businesses succeed where large companies fail. Take local bookstores. Ten years ago, many people predicted online retailers would close them all. Instead, a lot of independent bookstores are doing well. Why? They offer something online shops can't: personal recommendations from staff, author events and a sense of community. In other words, they stopped competing on price and started competing on experience.

ask.s: What did many people predict ten years ago?
ask.zh: 十年前很多人預測什麼？
ask.en: What did many people predict ten years ago?

options.t: Online retailers would close local bookstores.

explain.zh: 「網路零售商會讓書店全部倒閉」。

ask.s: What do independent bookstores offer that online shops cannot?
ask.zh: 獨立書店提供什麼網路商店做不到的？
ask.en: What do independent bookstores offer that online shops cannot?

explain.zh: 「店員的個人推薦、作家活動和社群感」。

ask.s: What is the professor's main point?
ask.zh: 教授的重點是什麼？
ask.en: What is the professor's main point?

options.t: Small businesses can succeed by offering an experience.
Price is the most important factor.

explain.zh: 「不再拚價格，而是拚體驗」。

lines.s: Have you registered for next semester's classes yet?

lines.en: Have you registered for next semester's classes yet?

options.t: I took that class last year.
options.en: I took that class last year.

options.t: Not yet — the system opens tomorrow.
options.en: Not yet — the system opens tomorrow.

explain.zh: 問登記了沒，回答「還沒，系統明天開放」。

lines.s: Do you know where the biology department moved to?
lines.zh: 你知道生物系搬到哪裡了嗎？
lines.en: Do you know where the biology department moved to?

options.t: It's in the new science building now.
options.en: It's in the new science building now.

options.zh: 生物是我最喜歡的科目。

options.t: I have a test in biology.
options.en: I have a test in biology.

explain.zh: 問搬到哪，回答地點。

lines.s: I'm thinking of joining the debate team.
lines.zh: 我在考慮加入辯論隊。
lines.en: I'm thinking of joining the debate team.

options.t: You'd be great — you love arguing!
options.zh: 妳一定很棒，妳超愛辯的！
options.en: You'd be great — you love arguing!

explain.zh: 對方考慮加入，鼓勵她最自然。

lines.s: Could you save me a seat at the lecture?
lines.zh: 妳可以在講座幫我留個位子嗎？
lines.en: Could you save me a seat at the lecture?

options.t: Sure, I'll sit near the front.
options.en: Sure, I'll sit near the front.

explain.zh: 請求留位子，答應「當然」。

lines.s: The cafeteria stopped serving breakfast after nine.
lines.zh: 餐廳九點後就不供應早餐了。
lines.en: The cafeteria stopped serving breakfast after nine.

options.t: Then I'd better get up earlier.
options.en: Then I'd better get up earlier.

explain.zh: 聽到消息，回應「那我最好早點起床」。

lines.s: How did your interview for the internship go?
lines.zh: 妳的實習面試怎麼樣？
lines.en: How did your interview for the internship go?

options.t: It was in the main office.
options.en: It was in the main office.

options.t: They're going to call me next week.
options.en: They're going to call me next week.

explain.zh: 問結果，回答「他們下週會打給我」。

lines.s: Is the professor's office hour on Tuesday or Wednesday?
lines.zh: 教授的辦公室時間是星期二還是星期三？
lines.en: Is the professor's office hour on Tuesday or Wednesday?

explain.zh: 選擇疑問句，選一個回答；不能用 Yes。

lines.s: I lost my notes from the history seminar.
lines.zh: 我把歷史研討課的筆記弄丟了。
lines.en: I lost my notes from the history seminar.

explain.zh: 對方弄丟筆記，提供「抄我的」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the housing office.
lines.zh: 請聽一段學生和宿舍辦公室職員的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the housing office.

lines.s: Hi, I'd like to change rooms. My roommate and I have very different schedules — she studies until three in the morning.
lines.zh: 你好，我想換房間。我和室友作息差很多，她讀書讀到凌晨三點。
lines.en: Hi, I'd like to change rooms. My roommate and I have very different schedules — she studies until three in the morning.

lines.s: I understand. Unfortunately, all the single rooms are taken this semester. But there's a double room available on the second floor.
lines.zh: 我了解。可惜這學期單人房都滿了，不過二樓有一間雙人房空著。
lines.en: I understand. Unfortunately, all the single rooms are taken this semester. But there's a double room available on the second floor.

lines.s: Who's the other student in that room?
lines.zh: 那間的另一位學生是誰？
lines.en: Who's the other student in that room?

lines.s: A first-year student who's on the swim team, so she goes to bed early for morning practice.
lines.zh: 一位一年級學生，是游泳隊的，早上要練習所以很早睡。
lines.en: A first-year student who's on the swim team, so she goes to bed early for morning practice.

ask.s: Why does the student want to change rooms?
ask.zh: 學生為什麼想換房間？
ask.en: Why does the student want to change rooms?

options.t: Her roommate keeps very late hours.
She wants a single room for studying.

explain.zh: 「她讀書讀到凌晨三點」。

ask.s: Why might the available room suit the student?
ask.zh: 那間空房為什麼可能適合她？
ask.en: Why might the available room suit the student?

options.t: It is on the first floor.
The other student goes to bed early.

explain.zh: 游泳隊學生「很早睡」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.
lines.zh: 請聽一段學生和教授的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.

lines.s: Professor Kim, I'd like to write my final paper on renewable energy in island communities. Is that too narrow?
lines.zh: 金教授，我想把期末報告寫成島嶼社區的再生能源，題目會太窄嗎？
lines.en: Professor Kim, I'd like to write my final paper on renewable energy in island communities. Is that too narrow?

lines.s: Not at all — narrow is good. But make sure you can find enough data. Have you checked the library's database?
lines.zh: 一點也不，窄很好。但要確定找得到足夠的資料。你查過圖書館的資料庫了嗎？
lines.en: Not at all — narrow is good. But make sure you can find enough data. Have you checked the library's database?

lines.s: Not yet. I was planning to use mainly news articles.
lines.zh: 還沒，我原本打算主要用新聞報導。
lines.en: Not yet. I was planning to use mainly news articles.

lines.s: News articles are fine for background, but you'll need peer-reviewed studies for your main argument.
lines.zh: 新聞報導當背景可以，但主要論點需要同儕審查的研究。
lines.en: News articles are fine for background, but you'll need peer-reviewed studies for your main argument.

ask.s: What is the professor's opinion of the topic?
ask.zh: 教授對題目的看法？
ask.en: What is the professor's opinion of the topic?

options.t: It's a good topic if there is enough data.
It has been done too often.

explain.zh: 「窄很好。但要確定找得到足夠的資料」。

ask.s: What does the professor advise?
ask.zh: 教授建議什麼？
ask.en: What does the professor advise?

options.t: Using academic studies for the main argument

explain.zh: 「主要論點需要同儕審查的研究」。

lines.s: Listen to a conversation between two students.
lines.zh: 請聽一段兩個學生的對話。
lines.en: Listen to a conversation between two students.

lines.s: Are you going to the career workshop on Friday?
lines.zh: 你星期五要去職涯工作坊嗎？
lines.en: Are you going to the career workshop on Friday?

lines.s: I want to, but I have a chemistry lab until four.
lines.zh: 想去，但我有化學實驗課到四點。
lines.en: I want to, but I have a chemistry lab until four.

lines.s: It doesn't start until four thirty, and it's in the student center, right next to the lab building.
lines.zh: 它四點半才開始，在學生中心，就在實驗大樓旁邊。
lines.en: It doesn't start until four thirty, and it's in the student center, right next to the lab building.

lines.s: Oh, then I can make it. Do we need to register?
lines.zh: 喔，那我趕得上。要報名嗎？
lines.en: Oh, then I can make it. Do we need to register?

lines.s: Yes, online — and only fifty spots, so do it today.
lines.zh: 要，線上報名，只有五十個名額，今天就報吧。
lines.en: Yes, online — and only fifty spots, so do it today.

ask.s: What was the man's concern about the workshop?

ask.en: What was the man's concern about the workshop?

ask.s: Why does the woman tell the man to register today?
ask.zh: 女的為什麼要他今天報名？
ask.en: Why does the woman tell the man to register today?

options.t: The number of places is limited.

explain.zh: 「只有五十個名額」。

lines.zh: 請聽一段校園廣播。
lines.en: Listen to an announcement on a university campus.

lines.zh: 同學請注意。因為施工，北停車場本月剩下的時間關閉。有停車證的學生可改停體育場停車場，早上七點到晚上七點每十分鐘有免費接駁車開往主校區。

ask.s: Why is the north parking lot closed?
ask.zh: 北停車場為什麼關閉？
ask.en: Why is the north parking lot closed?

explain.zh: 「因為施工」。

ask.s: What is provided for students?
ask.zh: 提供學生什麼？
ask.en: What is provided for students?

explain.zh: 「免費接駁車」。

lines.s: Listen to an announcement in a class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段課堂上的宣布。
lines.en: Listen to an announcement in a class.

lines.s: Before we begin, a quick change to the schedule. Next week's guest speaker, a journalist from the city newspaper, can only come on Thursday, so our Tuesday class is canceled and we'll meet on Thursday at the same time. Please read the two articles I posted online before then — she'll be discussing them.
lines.zh: 開始之前，課表有個小變動。下週的客座講者是市報的記者，她只有星期四能來，所以星期二的課取消，星期四同一時間上課。請在那之前讀完我貼在網路上的兩篇文章，她會討論它們。
lines.en: Before we begin, a quick change to the schedule. Next week's guest speaker, a journalist from the city newspaper, can only come on Thursday, so our Tuesday class is canceled and we'll meet on Thursday at the same time. Please read the two articles I posted online before then — she'll be discussing them.

ask.s: Why is Tuesday's class canceled?
ask.zh: 星期二的課為什麼取消？
ask.en: Why is Tuesday's class canceled?

options.t: A guest can only come on Thursday.

explain.zh: 「她只有星期四能來」。

ask.s: What should students do before the class?
ask.zh: 學生上課前要做什麼？
ask.en: What should students do before the class?

explain.zh: 「讀完我貼在網路上的兩篇文章」。

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段生物課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

lines.s: Today let's look at how some animals survive winter without eating. Many people think hibernation is just a long sleep, but it's quite different. When an animal like a ground squirrel hibernates, its body temperature can drop to near freezing, and its heart rate slows from about two hundred beats a minute to fewer than ten. This saves enormous amounts of energy. Interestingly, hibernating squirrels wake up briefly every couple of weeks, which actually uses a lot of their stored fat. Scientists aren't entirely sure why they do this, but one theory is that it allows their immune system to work properly.
lines.zh: 今天來看有些動物如何不吃東西度過冬天。很多人以為冬眠只是長時間睡覺，其實很不一樣。像地松鼠冬眠時，體溫可降到接近冰點，心跳從每分鐘約兩百下降到不到十下，省下大量能量。有趣的是，冬眠的松鼠每隔一兩週會短暫醒來，這其實會用掉很多儲存的脂肪。科學家不完全確定原因，有一種理論是這讓牠們的免疫系統正常運作。
lines.en: Today let's look at how some animals survive winter without eating. Many people think hibernation is just a long sleep, but it's quite different. When an animal like a ground squirrel hibernates, its body temperature can drop to near freezing, and its heart rate slows from about two hundred beats a minute to fewer than ten. This saves enormous amounts of energy. Interestingly, hibernating squirrels wake up briefly every couple of weeks, which actually uses a lot of their stored fat. Scientists aren't entirely sure why they do this, but one theory is that it allows their immune system to work properly.

ask.s: What point does the professor make about hibernation?
ask.zh: 教授對冬眠提出什麼觀點？
ask.en: What point does the professor make about hibernation?

options.t: It is the same as a long sleep.
It is very different from ordinary sleep.

explain.zh: 「很多人以為……只是長時間睡覺，其實很不一樣」。

ask.s: What happens to a ground squirrel's heart rate during hibernation?
ask.zh: 冬眠時地松鼠的心跳怎樣？
ask.en: What happens to a ground squirrel's heart rate during hibernation?

options.t: It drops to fewer than ten beats a minute.

explain.zh: 「從約兩百下降到不到十下」。

ask.s: Why does the professor mention the immune system?
ask.zh: 教授為什麼提到免疫系統？
ask.en: Why does the professor mention the immune system?

options.t: To offer a possible reason for brief waking
To explain how squirrels find food

explain.zh: 短暫醒來的原因「有一種理論是……免疫系統」。

lines.s: Listen to part of a lecture in an economics class.
lines.zh: 請聽一段經濟學課的講課。
lines.en: Listen to part of a lecture in an economics class.

lines.s: Let's talk about why prices often end in ninety-nine cents. It might seem silly — the difference between nine ninety-nine and ten dollars is just one cent. But studies show that customers read prices from left to right and pay most attention to the first digit. So nine ninety-nine feels closer to nine than to ten. This is called the left-digit effect. Interestingly, luxury stores often avoid ninety-nine endings, because round numbers signal quality rather than a bargain.
lines.zh: 我們來談為什麼價格常以九十九分結尾。看起來很蠢，九塊九十九和十塊只差一分錢。但研究顯示顧客從左往右讀價格，最注意第一個數字，所以九塊九十九感覺比較接近九而不是十。這叫左位數效應。有趣的是，精品店常避免用九十九結尾，因為整數傳達的是品質而不是便宜。
lines.en: Let's talk about why prices often end in ninety-nine cents. It might seem silly — the difference between nine ninety-nine and ten dollars is just one cent. But studies show that customers read prices from left to right and pay most attention to the first digit. So nine ninety-nine feels closer to nine than to ten. This is called the left-digit effect. Interestingly, luxury stores often avoid ninety-nine endings, because round numbers signal quality rather than a bargain.

ask.s: What is the lecture mainly about?
ask.zh: 這段講課主要是關於什麼？
ask.en: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.t: Why prices often end in ninety-nine

explain.zh: 講價格為什麼以九十九結尾。

ask.s: According to the professor, what do customers focus on?
ask.zh: 教授說顧客注意什麼？
ask.en: According to the professor, what do customers focus on?

options.t: The first digit of a price

explain.zh: 「最注意第一個數字」。

ask.s: Why do luxury stores avoid ninety-nine endings?
ask.zh: 精品店為什麼避免九十九結尾？
ask.en: Why do luxury stores avoid ninety-nine endings?

explain.zh: 「整數傳達的是品質」。
